covers: A child: mental functions with the child support checkboxes, medication supervision, a different set of grid items than the original note, plus speaking.
notes: To whom it may concern,
I am this child's pediatrician and have followed them since birth in 2017. They were diagnosed in 2019 with autism
spectrum disorder (level 3, requiring very substantial support) and intellectual disability.
Communication: the child is minimally verbal, with about 20 single words. They cannot make themselves understood by
anyone outside the family, even with their picture exchange system (PECS) and speech-generating device. This is the case
all or substantially all of the time. Speech has been impaired since the 2019 diagnosis, this has lasted more than
12 months, and it is not expected to improve. They attend speech-language therapy weekly.
Medication: risperidone for severe irritability and aggression. The parents give and supervise every dose.
It is mildly effective.
Other therapy: applied behaviour analysis 20 hours per week, occupational therapy, and visual schedules.
Independence: compared with other children of the same age, the child needs far more support.
They require one-to-one adult supervision at home at all times.
At school they have a full-time educational assistant and an individualized education plan.
Mental function ratings compared to peers:
- Adapting to change: severe limitations
- Expressing basic needs: severe limitations
- Awareness of danger (runs into traffic): severe limitations
- Regulation of behaviour: severe limitations
- Understanding verbal information: some limitations
- Basic hygiene and toileting: some limitations
Because of these limitations the child is unable, or takes an inordinate amount of time, to perform the mental functions
needed for everyday life, all or substantially all of the time. This began in 2019 and has lasted more than 12 months.
It is uncertain whether these mental functions will improve.
Medical records are on file. I have been the child's physician from 2017 to present.
